title: Erdős #740 and the r → ∞ Extreme
content: Erdős–Hajnal Problem #740 asks whether a graph G of infinite chromatic number 𝔪 must, for each r ≥ 1, contain a subgraph of chromatic number 𝔪 with no odd cycle of length ≤ r. Rödl (1982) settled 𝔪 = ℵ₀, r = 3; the general problem is open and Erdős listed it among those he most wanted solved. The parameter r interpolates: r = 3 forbids triangles, and r = ∞ forbids odd cycles of every length — which is exactly bipartiteness. This file studies the r = ∞ extreme honestly with Mathlib's real chromatic number, after the parent file Erdos740Problem.lean used a placeholder (Cardinal.mk V) that made its statements vacuous.
mathContext: $\chi(G) = \mathfrak{m}$ infinite, $r \ge 1$: does $G$ contain a subgraph with $\chi = \mathfrak{m}$ and no odd cycle of length $\le r$? Here $r = \infty \iff$ the subgraph is bipartite.

title: Real Chromatic Numbers and the Two Structural Lemmas
content: The parent file defined chromaticNumber V G := Cardinal.mk V — a placeholder equal to the vertex count, unrelated to colourings — so its open no_infinite_bipartite sorry was not a statement about χ at all. This file uses Mathlib's genuine ℕ∞-valued SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber and IsBipartite := Colorable 2. Two real structural lemmas carry everything: induce_chromaticNumber_le shows the inclusion G.induce s ↪g G is a graph homomorphism, so by chromaticNumber_mono_of_hom an induced subgraph never raises χ; bipartite_chromaticNumber_le_two unfolds IsBipartite to Colorable 2 and applies Colorable.chromaticNumber_le to get χ ≤ 2.
mathContext: $\chi(G.\mathrm{induce}\,s) \le \chi(G)$ (monotone under the inclusion homomorphism) and $G\text{ bipartite} \Rightarrow \chi(G) \le 2$.

title: The r = ∞ Extreme of #740 Is False
content: no_bipartite_induced_realizes_chromatic shows the bipartite extreme fails: if χ(G) > 2, no induced bipartite subgraph H can have χ(H) = χ(G), because bipartiteness forces χ(H) ≤ 2 < χ(G) — a one-line contradiction (heq ▸ bipartite_chromaticNumber_le_two then not_le). The whole obstruction is the elementary bound χ(bipartite) ≤ 2: there is simply no bipartite subgraph of large chromatic number to find. bipartite_induced_chromaticNumber_le_two isolates the reusable structural fact. This is the honest theorem the placeholder file's sorry was reaching for.

title: Chromatic Numbers of the Complete Graphs
content: triangle_chromaticNumber and completeGraph_chromaticNumber compute χ(Kₙ) = |Fin n| = n via Mathlib's chromaticNumber_top (the chromatic number of the complete graph ⊤ on a finite vertex type is the number of vertices). In particular χ(K₃) = 3. These supply the χ > 2 hypothesis of no_bipartite_induced_realizes_chromatic for concrete graphs, turning the abstract failure into checkable instances.

title: Non-Vacuous Witnesses and the Real Content of #740
content: triangle_has_no_bipartite_realization and completeGraph_has_no_bipartite_realization (n ≥ 3) feed the computed chromatic numbers into the failure theorem, exhibiting explicit graphs whose chromatic number cannot be realized on any bipartite induced subgraph. The triangle already witnesses it (χ = 3 > 2). Making the failure concrete and non-vacuous delimits the genuine content of Erdős #740 to the FINITE-r regime — where Rödl's r = 3, 𝔪 = ℵ₀ theorem lives and the general problem remains open — rather than the trivially-false r = ∞ extreme.
mathContext: For $n \ge 3$, $K_n$ has $\chi = n > 2$, so no bipartite induced subgraph realizes $\chi(K_n)$ — the $r = \infty$ case fails non-vacuously.
